**In one line**: Anthropic is reported to have introduced a "Model Hardware Standard" that links AI agents to real machines and hardware.

### Key points
- The standard is described as a spec that lets AI agents move beyond software to **directly control physical devices, robots, and industrial equipment**.
- It reads as an effort to extend the existing pattern of agents connecting to software tools (such as MCP) into the physical-hardware domain.
- Detailed specifications and supported scope appear to be at an early stage, with limited real-world deployments so far.

### Why it matters
AI agents have mostly operated on screen. If a hardware-control standard takes hold, manufacturing, logistics, and robotics could move toward AI "physically operating machines" — while raising the stakes on safety, permissions, and accountability at the same time.
